reason: The cited evidence supports that active learning yields accurate ML potentials for refractory high-entropy alloys (E1, E2) and that vibrational entropy can be extracted from atomic displacements (E3), but none of the passages address transfer learning for electron–vibration coupling, free-energy integration in liquids, or the claimed order-of-magnitude speedup relative to TOR-TILD.
premises: ML potentials trained on ab initio data can reach near-DFT accuracy for multicomponent alloys
Active learning tailors training sets to specific systems and properties, minimizing DFT calculations
ML potentials can capture anharmonic effects and vibrational entropy in solids and liquids
Transfer learning can refine ML potentials to capture electron–vibration coupling
ML-based free-energy integration reduces computational cost by an order of magnitude vs. AIMD/TOR-TILD
